plan: This is effectively a second-price auction structure: my sealed bid acts as my maximum willingness to pay, and I'll only pay the second-highest bid if I win. Bidding my true value ($46) is the dominant strategy here - if I bid higher, I risk winning and overpaying relative to my value; if I bid lower, I risk losing profitable auctions I should have won. Truthful bidding maximizes expected profit regardless of others' strategies.

In this ascending clock auction with sealed exit bids, the mechanism is equivalent to a second-price auction: I pay the second-highest bid if I win, not my own bid. Bidding my true value ($17) is the dominant strategy - it maximizes expected profit since bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth, and bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. I'll bid exactly my value.

Since this mechanism is equivalent to a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win, determined by my sealed bid acting as my exit point), the dominant strategy is to bid my true value. Bidding higher risks overpaying, bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. Therefore, I will bid exactly $28, my true value, to maximize expected profit.
